lines.japanese:
朝の光を感じる。
　まぶたを閉じて眠りに落ちていても、柔らかな陽射しは混濁する意識を目覚めさせようとする。
―――意識が、だんだんと自分を取り戻す。
　静かな雰囲気。
　空気はほどよく冷たく、陽射しはそれを緩和するぐらいに温かい。
　どうやら、今日はこれ以上ないっていうぐらいいい天気みたいだ。
lines.label: s200
lines.maoEnglish:
I feel the morning light.
Though my eyes are closed and I am sunk in sleep, the gentle sun coaxes my muddled consciousness toward waking.
―――Little by little, my awareness becomes my own again.
Everything is quiet.
The air is pleasantly cool, while the sun is warm enough to soften its chill.
It seems today is going to be as beautiful as any day could possibly be.

---Slowly, I start to awaken.

I guess the weather will be great today.

　体はベッドに横たわっていて、枕元にはメガネがある。

lines.maoEnglish:
“…”
I wake.
I’m lying in bed, my glasses beside the pillow.
Without thinking, I put them on and let my gaze drift around the room.
The sunlight pouring through the window is so pure it seems to whisper, Come on.
“…”
I breathe out softly.
Fresh air fills my lungs, washing the inside of my chest clean.

―――――それは、紛れもなく平穏な日常だ。
「……………」

Birds call from the woods outside.
I lie in my warm bed, doing nothing, immersed in the slow passage of time.
―――――This is unmistakably a peaceful, ordinary life.
“…”
And yet I find it faintly unsatisfying.
Even though I’ve returned to such a pristine morning, something in me feels strangely out of place.

“The news said that a woman―――a girl our age, actually, went shopping last night and never came home. Apparently her family lives near the park.”
“I see. Near the park, then.”
The moment I said it, the contents of my stomach surged toward my throat.

「なんだ、おまえますます不健康になってくな。
そんなに新しい生活は合わないのか？」
「ああ、そうなのかもしれないな。
　朝は七時に起きても遅いと文句は言われるし、門限は八時だし。
おまけに無断外泊すると厳しく詰問されるなんて、監獄生活みたいだろ？」
「いいじゃねえか、規則正しい生活で。
管理体制万万歳、若者はもっとタイトに生きねえとな。
若いうちから楽しちゃろくな大人になれないぞ」
「同感。
……けど、有彦に言われると誰に言われるより説得力があるね」
　その、究極的な反面教師として。
lines.label: s227
lines.maoEnglish:
“You look less healthy every day. Does your new life disagree with you that much?”
“Maybe it does.
They complain that seven is late to wake up, impose an eight o’clock curfew, and interrogate me if I spend a night away without permission. Sounds like prison, doesn’t it?”
“What’s wrong with that? Long live strict supervision; young people ought to live with a little discipline. Take it easy while you’re young and you’ll never grow into a decent adult.”
“Agreed. Somehow, coming from you, that carries more weight than it would from anyone else.”
As the ultimate cautionary example.

　……我ながらこの素直すぎる発言はどうかと思うんだけど、性格なので変えようがない。
　先輩はくすり、と小さく笑ってまっすぐに俺の目を見つめると、
「遠野くんって、達観してる」
　なんて、すごく優しい声で言った。

“Is the lunch good?”
“Mmm, it’s cold, so not especially.”
Even I suspect that answer may be too honest, but that is simply how I am.
She laughs softly, meets my eyes, and
“You really are a little sage, aren’t you?”
she says in a remarkably gentle voice.

I would have preferred a dashing young master in traditional dress, but when she says it, even retired gentleman does not sound so bad.

　首をかしげながら正門に向かう。
　と、翡翠はこちらに気がついて、ペコリと頭をさげてきた。

　さも当然のように、翡翠は眉ひとつ動かさずに言ってくる。

“―――Ah, right―――I’m home, Hisui.”

“Um―――were you waiting here for me to come back?”
“Yes. It is a servant’s duty to welcome home the master of the house.”
Hisui says it as though it were obvious, without so much as raising an eyebrow.
